name: Mand
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Daniels, Don R. 2015. A Reconstruction of Proto-Sogeram. PhD dissertation, UC Santa Barbara (covers Mand/Atemble phonology); also Daniels 2020 Grammatical Reconstruction (De Gruyter).

sources.citation: Daniels, Don. 2021. Curriculum Vitae (Sept 2021), publication list.
sources.note: Bibliographic only: confirms no Mand-specific phonology paper exists; lists Daniels 2010 (Oceanic Linguistics 49(1):163-193) and Daniels 2020 (De Gruyter) as the other Sogeram phonology/grammar works.

sources.citation: Daniels, Don Roger. 2015. A Reconstruction of Proto-Sogeram: Phonology, Lexicon, and Morphosyntax. PhD dissertation, University of California, Santa Barbara. Appendix 1 'Mand Grammar Sketch' pp. 439-536 (phonology sec. 1.2 pp. 443-447, PDF pp. 468-472); sec. 2.2.2 'Mand Innovations' pp. 69-74.
sources.note: Nothing on where Mand stress falls. Phonology sec. 1.2 (pp. 443-447) covers consonants, vowels, allophony of /a/ /z/ and prenasalized stops, status of /w y ɨ/, vowel elision; no word stress, accent or tone. Only remark: sec. 2.2.2.3 p. 72 (PDF p. 97) 'Further research into the stress systems of the Sogeram languages might reveal a consistent pattern.' Whole-text search for stress/accent/tone/prosody: no other word-level hit.
Nothing; speaker numbers (8 fluent speakers in 2014), fieldwork dates, contact history only.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, John A. 1980. A comparative word list of the Southern Adelbert Range languages, Madang Province, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics D-33. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Nothing; semi-phonemic comparative wordlist without stress marks; the word 'stress' does not occur in the text layer.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, John A. 1971. Classificatory and typological studies in languages of the Madang District. Pacific Linguistics C-19. Canberra: ANU. Atemple = language 41/At, sec. 2.22.41.11 p. 62; Atan Family typology sec. 2.22.41.3 p. 63; Wanang Stock typology sec. 2.22.45 pp. 64-65.
sources.note: Nothing for Atemple: phoneme-level typological features only (alveopalatal stops, prenasalized voiced stops, /l/ and /r/ not contrastive in Atemple, high-central vowel). General p. 13: 'The marking of stress has been omitted, since the stress patterning has not been well established yet.'

sources.citation: Z'graggen, John A. 1969. Classificatory and typological studies in languages of the Western Madang District, New Guinea. PhD thesis, Australian National University (hdl 1885/130077). Atemple sec. 2.22.41.11 p. 109.
sources.note: Nothing; same content as the 1971 book (adds that Fr. Ziegler SVD's early Atemple materials were lost). Stress omitted from all wordlists (pp. 13-14, same sentence as 1971).
